title: 📖 04 — Magic & the Cosmos
rawNotionMarkup: Edition II continuity and provenance note. This chapter is the complete available Notion reference from 20 November 2026, retained as the detailed starting text rather than condensed. It remains revisable by its creator. Review the evidence-status guardrails below; the original Bible and chat export may provide later additions. ## Edition II continuity guardrails - The world has Natural Magic, lunar influences and other established magical traditions. Their interaction has rules and risks; no instant proficiency, guaranteed spell outcome or arbitrary moon affinity. - Lost Natural Magic harmonisation is a broader ancient technique, not exclusively a First Throne or Khazari invention. Gloin has not discovered its mechanism; his Common/Natural Magic hypothesis is his own and Elska's research is a separate unpublished assignment. - Gloin's aptitude and sensitive stone experiences are not demonstrated mastery, conscious mountain contact, ancestral recognition or a predetermined heroic destiny. - The incomplete lunar catastrophe chronology and individual moon orbital numbers remain open, despite the physical canon of a complex moon-and-ring system. Direct source: Magic & the Cosmos. Historical source: The Eryndor World Bible. --- ## Source-recovered Day 19 preliminary magical sensitivity test — distinct from later controlled tests At the Silver Anvil on Autumn Day 19, Year 3,847, before a messenger's 3:06 PM arrival, Maela Deepforge carried out a three-material screening. She warned Gloin not to force a magical effect: it was an observation of response to materials, not a test of mastery. 1. Ancient-rune black iron: Gloin initially felt nothing, then a faint vibration ran from palm to forearm when he relaxed and concentrated; the engraved rune faintly lit. Maela stopped and examined it. 2. Binding-inscribed copper disc: Gloin felt almost nothing, an important negative control. 3. Smooth mountain crystal: Gloin felt a subtle sensation similar to the iron response. Maela tested it herself and observed a different result, with no quantified reading supplied. Maela described a possible sensitivity to stone-bound runic energy, termed Deep Resonance in this aptitude context. It suggested some sensitivity in Runecraft and a promising possibility in Deepcraft. Forgebinding, Hearthmagic, Stonecalling and Ancestral Binding were untested at this exact stage. The sensitivity might be innate or particular to an enchantment; one examination established no mastery, reliable Stonecalling, magical identity, hidden ancestry or guaranteed destiny. Maela specifically said a similar response had led some people to mastery and another to no useful achievement. Do not conflate this preliminary screening with later controlled tests involving an ancient rune's heartbeat-like sensation, a broken rune's cold section or the glow from a disconnected binding stone. Later assessments describe stronger potential, but should not be retroactively inserted into the Day 19 test. Terminological guardrail: “Deep Resonance” here is Maela's description of a possible personal sensitivity and must not be automatically identified with the ancient historical Deep Resonance episode of the Silence Below. A common phrase does not prove a shared mechanism. Original offer: Maela proposed a flexible provisional apprenticeship, including Khazari script, two lessons per week as schedules permitted, identification of magical materials, further examinations, and no immediate fee for the first month. Formal apprenticeship could be negotiated afterward; Gloin was not automatically trained or enlisted. The subsequently accepted apprenticeship in the Characters ledger remains a later state in the chronology. ## Day 20, 5:50–6:35 PM — script study and the distinction between literacy and mastery In the original-play text, Gloin opened Hadrik's borrowed The Foundations of First Throne Script, copied and studied twelve introductory symbols, practised their forms and pronunciations, and by the end of the session could recognise all twelve, with some still demanding thought. The narrator also noted that certain symbols changed meaning in context. One sign meaning “maintain” resembled a marking in the eastern mine's outer containment ring; this is an observed resemblance, not proof of the marking's actual function or any established identity with “Hold”. Twelve visually recognised is not twelve magically learned or mastered. Gloin had not been shown performing runework using those twelve symbols. His later three introductory symbols in active practical instruction remain Hold, Within and Until Command, consistent with book-study of a larger set. Do not erase the 12-symbol study scene or upgrade it into practical Runecraft mastery. Maela's prior Day 19 three-material test likewise proved neither full Runecraft capability nor Stonecalling. ## Complete topic reference — preserved from the preceding edition This page records Eryndor's underlying magical principles, the natural satellite system, recognised disciplines, Khazari traditions, everyday magic and the lost ancient art of Natural Magic harmonisation. The rules below apply across the world; individual cultures and schools interpret and practise them differently. ## No extinctions at the Second Age-ending earthquake catastrophe; magic's protective role unresolved (creator direction, 21 November 2026) HARD CREATOR RULE — NO EXTINCTIONS: The extreme planetwide earthquakes that ended the Second Age (Year 1,437), the ancient Ironspine ring's tenfold global aftershock amplification, and the almost instantaneous violent raising of marshlands and lowlands did NOT cause the extinction of any entire race or species. Every people survived somewhere in Eryndor. This is not a minor casualty event: deaths could be enormous, the worst directly uplifted communities had no time to flee, and individual towns, districts, settlements, cultural communities and regional societies could be overwhelmed or destroyed. No entire species is wiped out. Do not introduce a vanished “last of their kind” race, extinct biological species, or world-level people extinction to dramatize the quake. Creator's developing magic idea: A magical force will play some part in the survival of the peoples and the prevention of extinction. This is an explicit direction for future worldbuilding, NOT a settled magical mechanism or fully described historical episode. Its identity, origin, capabilities, degree and manner of influence, timing, whether it acts intentionally, who knows about it, and whether it relates to Lunar Magic, the independent World's Breath, gods of magic, the Ironspine Mountains, or something else are all UNDECIDED. Do not automatically make it a global protective barrier, time reversal, immortality, a moon deity's act, or an unexplained universal resurrection. The magic's contribution must be reconciled eventually with the immense deaths and near-zero warning. This note does not establish that people understood its role at the time. Era boundary and protected gaps: This is canon about the event ending the Second Age and beginning the Third Age, now complemented by the creator-authorized regional cultural and political history of the 116-year Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), recorded in Era of Fire — Kingdoms, Peoples & Cultural Chronicle (Second Age, 1322–1437). The race-specific Awakening (Years 1–321) and Wonder (Years 322–1,321) histories remain intact, as do permanent losses of certain moon-specific magical disciplines (which are NOT species extinctions) caused at the end of the First Age. First Throne involvement in any Age transition is still only an optional undetermined storyline, not a factual claim. No present population census changes or new species ancestry is implied. ## Era of Wonder — mastery of new moon-born magic and renewed global prosperity (creator canon, 21 November 2026) DEFINING HISTORICAL CHARACTER — APPROVED: The 1,000-year Era of Wonder, the second era of the Second Age (Years 322–1,321 inclusive), was an era of new magical mastery, widespread prosperity, and a great resurgence of magic across the entire globe of Eryndor. After the preceding 321-year Era of Awakening's darkness, confusion, devastation, and magical instability, peoples increasingly learned to understand, harness, stabilize in practice, and master new lunar magics created when shards of shattered original moons became new moons after the First Great Cataclysm. A flourishing civilization-building period followed, with greater confidence in magic, sustained experimentation, magical knowledge, new applications and widespread social/economic flourishing. The darkness and confusion of the first era were largely overcome; it was time for magic to rise again worldwide. The renewed magic is new, NOT recovered First Age magic: Many original moon-derived forms of magic were permanently and irrevocably lost because their source-moons ceased to exist; only First Age peoples could ever have experienced some of them and no First Age records survive. The Era of Wonder's achievements came from mastering emergent fragment-moon magics and continuing viable older, culturally distinct magical traditions, not from reactivating vanished sources or reconstructing extinct disciplines. The planet's separate Natural Magic / World's Breath remained present; it does not become lunar magic. Do not assign particular new magical disciplines to named moons, invent named 'lost' spells, or erase existing Khazari, Eldar, Fae, Gnome and other established traditions. Worldwide renaissance with diverse societies: Prosperity and magical advances spread across Eryndor as a whole, not just Avarra or one race, state, faith, magical school or geopolitical power. Each region and people could develop distinctive approaches. The millennium is broadly prosperous and magically flourishing, but this is not a decree that every single year, kingdom, person or region was free of suffering, war, inequality or failed spells. Mastery means significant progress after the Awakening, not perfect infallibility of every spell or a retcon of the key lesson that societies should not depend on magic alone; practical engineering, craftsmanship, agriculture, records, and other mundane capacities continue alongside powerful magical work. Chronological safeguards: The Era of Wonder followed the Era of Awakening (Years 1–321) and ended before the 116-year Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). The third era concluded with global earthquakes which, after reaching Ironspine's ancient deep-running roots, were amplified tenfold planetwide and raised the separate far-western-tip Avarran mountains; that event ended the Second Age, not the Era of Wonder directly. The preceding Era of Wonder's named individuals and precise achievements remain largely unassigned. New local rulers and historical polities are now established for the following Era of Fire in its separate cultural chronicle; the precise cause of either era transition and any First Throne role remain open. Gloin's ancestry and paused campaign are untouched. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime during the Third Age. The exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, identities of the first communities, and subsequent structure of mage–Orc command remain UNDECIDED. The Orcs were absent from the Second Age's Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321) and Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). Earlier lore depicting Orc inhabitants, clans, armies, cities or events in either of those two Ages is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. CREATOR CANON — Third Age creation and intended conquests: The exiled dark mages who formed the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano during the Second Age survived well into the Third Age, when they created the Urakai (Orcs) by a method not yet decided. Their ambition in creating the Orcs was first to besiege the dwarven (Khazari) strongholds, and ultimately to attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This establishes the mages' intentions, not any particular siege, conquest, campaign, chronology, victory or attack as an accomplished fact. The mages established no diplomacy, trade, treaties or alliances with pre-existing outside peoples; creating the Orcs is an act of creation for the mages' ambitions, not evidence of diplomatic relations. The exact magical or other creation process, timing, first Orc settlements, degree and duration of mage control, and later independence or resistance remain open. The modern Urakai are a diverse people with their own cultures and agency; they are not collectively evil, personally culpable for the mages' acts, or necessarily still subject to their creators. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Dark mages and the Urakai (Orcs) — CREATION CONFIRMED IN THIRD AGE; MILITARY AMBITIONS ESTABLISHED (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR'S BINDING THIRD AGE HISTORY: The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age in pursuit of a planned war of conquest: besiege the Khazari dwarven strongholds first, then eventually attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This was an ambition and intended sequence, not confirmation that specific attacks or wars actually took place. Their creation technique, timing, organization of the first Orcs, later relationship to the mages, and historical results are intentionally not yet defined. The Orcs were wholly absent from the First and Second Ages. Existing binding facts: At the beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322), exiled mages created the southeastern Avarran wastes and their volcano using dark magic. At the close of the Second Age (Year 1,437), the global earthquakes intensified that volcano; the mages harnessed its energy to reduce volcanic devastation and unwittingly gained greater magical strength. The mages survived well into the Third Age and established NO relations with any outside peoples—no alliances, trade, diplomacy or cooperative ties. Modern southeastern Avarra includes substantial independent Urakai communities. Urakai are not universally evil, dark mages or participants in the mages' deliberate destruction by default. Open questions, NOT decided: By what magical or other means the dark mages created the first Orcs; the precise year and place within the Third Age; whether each mage participated or held equal authority; the numbers, first communities and abilities of created Orcs; whether and how the creators commanded them; whether the intended sieges and later attacks occurred, against which named strongholds or kingdoms, with what resistance and outcomes; and the emergence of independent Orc cultures over later generations. Do not fill these gaps automatically. The mages' earlier political and diplomatic isolation from existing outside peoples still stands: no unapproved treaties, trade, alliances or diplomatic partners. Present-day Urakai are distinct individuals and societies, not automatically loyal to ancient mages. Protected mysteries: Exact races/identities of the original mage groups are still unknown; the mages' ancestry and ultimate fate are open. No link to the First Throne, historical east–west wars, the original lunar catastrophe, or Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unpredetermined heritage is proved. Leave this thread available for later creator decisions without resolving it during campaign play or by editorial inference. ## Exiled dark mages — complete political and social isolation from outsiders (creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON — NO OUTSIDE RELATIONS: From their formation by outcast magical practitioners at the beginning of the Era of Fire, and during their established survival well into the Third Age, the dark-mage groups of the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes did not develop relations with anyone outside their own group. They established no diplomatic relations, trade ties, alliances, treaties or cooperative political relationships with neighboring peoples, polities or communities. Treat them as an isolated power that remained apart from other societies, not a regular participant in interregional commerce, diplomacy or political coalitions. Their internal organization, personal associations among exiles, and succession across generations remain open; this does not mean they had no community among themselves. Precision: This is a correction to earlier speculative language about the mages “developing relationships with surrounding peoples.” Such external relationships did not happen. Historical encounters, threats, conflicts or observations from outsiders are not automatically established or precluded by this statement; do not invent such events. Their knowledge, exact longevity, later fate, and whether their tradition survives to the Fifth Age remain unresolved. Do not attribute dark-mage deeds to all Urakai or other inhabitants of the larger southeastern badlands region. ## Era of Fire's ending — the mages harnessed the volcano and unknowingly grew in power (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CANON EVENT AT SECOND AGE → THIRD AGE: The exiled dark mages had created the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano through dark magic at the beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322). At the end of that era (Year 1,437), planetwide earthquakes, whose aftershocks were amplified tenfold across the globe by the ancient Ironspine mountain ring, intensified their magically created volcano. The mages harnessed the power of the volcano itself to keep it from erupting with the full potential destructive force it otherwise could have had. Their intervention reduced the severity of the volcanic catastrophe; it does not establish that there was no eruption at all, no damage, or no casualties. Unforeseen effect: In channeling and restraining that volcanic power, the dark mages unknowingly acquired even greater magical power themselves. This increase in their power is an established consequence of the containment effort, although they did not know or understand it at the time. The exact metaphysical mechanism, quantitative strength increase, whether every mage gained equally, and the time and manner of any later recognition remain unknown. Their continued presence well into the Third Age is established independently; the power gain is not automatically proved to be the sole reason they survived the worldwide disaster. Continuity: The volcano was created by dark magic at the start of the Era of Fire, and was intensified by global earthquakes at the end; the mages then contained some of its destructive power, inadvertently augmenting themselves. None of this constitutes friendly diplomacy, outside alliances or trade; the dark mages remained socially and politically isolated. The origins and exact identity of their dark magical source, the exact technique for harnessing a volcanic force, and their later Third Age history remain open. Nor is a connection to the First Throne or to the separately undefined species-survival magical force established. ## Dark-mage continuity — endured well into the Third Age (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW CHRONOLOGICAL FACT: The dark-mage groups exiled from their villages at the beginning of the 116-year Era of Fire, who banded together in the formerly fertile southeastern agricultural lands of Avarra and deliberately created the Southern Wastes and their volcano with dark magic, were NOT confined to the Second Age. These dark-mage groups, their communities and practice continued WELL INTO THE THIRD AGE. The global earthquakes at the end of the Second Age (Second Age Year 1,437) therefore did NOT end their existence as a continuing dark-mage presence. The volcano they had created early in the Era of Fire was also intensified by the ending earthquakes; creation and later intensification are distinct events. Do not overdefine the survival: “Lasted well into the Third Age” is an intentionally broad period, not a fixed number of years or confirmation that each individual founder survived that long. The continuance may encompass successive generations, settlements, groups or traditions; the precise institutions and continuity of named founders are unwritten. Do not assign exact Third Age dates, sovereigns, wars, bloodlines, defeats, religion, expanded borders, extinction, destruction, migration, or a confirmed Fifth Age continuation. Neither their disappearance nor their survival to the present has been established. Dark magic is not attributed to an entire race, and the southern Urakai civilizations cannot be cast as the perpetrators by species. Protected chronology: (1) Second Age Year 1,322 — dark-mage exiles unite, magically transform southeastern Avarran fertile farmland into the Southern Wastes and create its volcano; (2) Second Age Year 1,437 — planetwide earthquakes shake the world, amplified tenfold globally by ancient Ironspine and intensifying the previously created volcano, ending Second Age and beginning Third Age; (3) a significant but UNNUMBERED span well into the Third Age — the dark mages endure. How they survived the natural catastrophe or interacted with the separately established yet-unidentified magical force involved in preventing species extinction is not known. First Throne involvement is an open, noncanon story option; Gloin's ancestry is unchanged and unresolved. ## Era of Fire — exile of dark mages and magical creation of the Southern Wastes (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR-ESTABLISHED FOUNDING EVENT, NOT A PROPOSAL: At the very beginning of the Era of Fire, the third and final era of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age (beginning in Second Age Year 1,322), certain groups of mages found a way to practice newly accessed dark magic. They were cast out of their home villages because of their discovery or practice. The scattered exiles banded together in the southern lands. Those lands were NOT originally wastes: they had been fertile farming country with established agricultural communities. Deliberate transformation: At the outset of the Era of Fire, the united dark mages used their new-found dark magic to transform that fertile farmland into the bleak Southern Wastes, deliberately turning productive lands into a wasteland that became their own home. The devastation is an act of the exiled mage groups, not a natural original desert, not a consequence to be misassigned to the planetwide earthquakes at the END of the Era of Fire, and not a landform that had always been infertile. These are two separate established events at opposite ends of the 116-year era. Geographical identity — CREATOR NOW FIXED: “the Southern Wastes” created by the exiled dark mages are located on AVARRA, in the SOUTHEASTERN PART OF THE CREATOR'S APPROVED CONTINENT MAP, in the portion MARKED WITH A VOLCANO. This is NOT Sahrad and must NOT be merged with Sahrad's independently established Red Wastes, Glass Desert, or Sunscorched Expanse. This confirms that the formerly fertile farming country destroyed by the exiled mages at the opening of the Era of Fire occupies part of the southeastern volcanic/badlands region of Avarra. TWO-STAGE VOLCANO HISTORY — CREATOR CORRECTION: The volcano was CREATED by the exiled mages' DARK MAGIC at the very beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322), when they deliberately transformed fertile southeastern Avarran farmland into their Southern Wastes home. It did NOT exist before the dark-mage transformation and was not originally created by the earthquakes. However, at the END of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,437), the planetwide earthquakes and globally tenfold-amplified aftershocks intensified the ALREADY-EXISTING MAGICAL VOLCANO. Both events shaped its present state: magical creation first, seismic intensification later. The exact volcanic response (eruption frequency, magnitude, lava fields, ash, secondary effects), whether the first magical creation involved an eruption, and particular local casualties remain unspecified. Do not erase either the original dark-magic cause or the later earthquake-driven intensification, and do not automatically attribute the entire Southern Wastes' creation to the age-ending earthquake. Exact boundaries and the specific volcano's proper name have not been supplied; don't assume every southeastern badland, every volcanic zone, or all current Urakai territory was magically transformed. Respect the many established permanent Urakai, Goblin, Ogre, Kobold, Gnome and other communities of modern southeastern Avarra; do not make Urakai responsible for the mages' act by ethnicity or geography. Their urban and pastoral communities may survive among safe valleys, wells and habitable zones in the wider southeastern region. The modern sixfold census is not changed, nor are the names or locations of any existing settlements automatically reassigned. Magic and moral distinction: Eryndor already has intrinsically good, morally grey and intrinsically evil magics. This event confirms that these mage groups gained access to and used dark magic; it does NOT yet name a source moon, deity, magical discipline, patron, spell, ritual, unique innovation or specify whether that power itself was newly born at this moment rather than newly discovered/learned by the mages. Do not equate every mage, magic user, people or regional inhabitant with these exiles. Nor is the “fire” in the Era of Fire's name yet explicitly explained by this incident alone, unless the creator decides that. Unsettled details — do not fill automatically: Exact races and numbers of mages, identities and motivations of their villages, original names and states of the farming communities, how rapidly the land transformed, what happened to the farmers, whether any groups opposed the exiles, the detailed Third Age history of their enduring settlements and magical lineage (the groups are now established as surviving well into the Third Age, but their ultimate fate remains open), and whether the dark magic connects to the First Throne or later global earthquakes are all OPEN. Do not assert an extinct species or apply modern census values to ancient populations. The creator earlier restricted free-form invention in the third era, but has now directly authorized this specific event. This historical restriction was later superseded: the creator authorized detailed Era of Fire cultures, kingdoms, rulers and wars, which are now recorded in the Era of Fire chronicle and Second Age Annals. Do not invent an unapproved additional globe-wide catastrophe, a First Throne role, or specific dark-mage encounters. Era boundary protections: The Era of Fire lasted 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). Its ending global earthquakes reached the vastly older-than-First-Age Ironspine ring, whose central position and deep roots magnified their aftershocks tenfold across Eryndor; sudden lowland and marshland uplift (including far-western Avarran mountain creation) caused immense deaths but no species extinctions, with some protective contribution by a yet undefined magical force. The beginning dark-mage terraforming has NO established causal link to the ending earthquakes or extinction-prevention magic. The First Throne connection remains a speculative possibility, and Gloin's unknown ancestry and paused campaign are not changed. ## Era of Fire — third and final era of the Second Age, 116 years (creator canon, 21 November 2026) AVARRAN HISTORICAL NAME, CREATOR-ESTABLISHED: The third and final Avarran-defined era of Eryndor's Second Age is called the Era of Fire; other continents may name or divide the period differently. It lasted 116 years, corresponding to Second Age Years 1,322–1,437 inclusive. Its exact duration is derived from the already confirmed Second Age total: 1,437 − 321 years (Era of Awakening) − 1,000 years (Era of Wonder) = 116 years. Chronology: (1) Era of Awakening, Years 1–321, 321 years; (2) Era of Wonder, Years 322–1,321, 1,000 years; (3) Era of Fire, Years 1,322–1,437, 116 years. The catastrophic global earthquakes at the end of the Era of Fire ended the Second Age and began the Third Age. Their causes, seismic effects, sudden marshland and lowland mountain uplift, tenfold global aftershock amplification through the ancient Ironspine, mass deaths without whole-species extinction and the as-yet-undefined magical protection are recorded separately, not invented here. PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED INTERIOR — CREATOR UPDATE: The creator has now established an event at the very start of the Era of Fire: groups of mages who found access to dark magic were exiled from their villages, gathered in formerly fertile southern farming lands, and deliberately used dark magic to transform those lands into their new wasteland home (see the dedicated Era of Fire Southern Wastes section). The location in southeastern Avarra is established, and the creator has subsequently authorized new regional kingdoms, cultures and a limited non-Orc conflict described in Era of Fire — Kingdoms, Peoples & Cultural Chronicle (Second Age, 1322–1437). The dark mages' identities and magical techniques, the ultimate fates of new historical states, any further dragon cults or magical fire episodes, First Throne involvement and the cause of the final global earthquakes remain open. The meaning of the word “Fire” in the era's name is not yet conclusively pinned to this event. The First Throne remains a deliberately unresolved possible thread; Gloin's unknown ancestry and campaign scene remain unaffected. ## Era of Wonder — second era of the Second Age, 1,000 years (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW CHRONOLOGY — ESTABLISHED: The second of the Second Age's three successive eras was named the Era of Wonder and lasted exactly 1,000 years. It followed the 321-year Era of Awakening; using retrospective Second-Age year numbering, the Era of Wonder ran from Second Age Year 322 through Year 1,321, inclusive. Reconciled Second Age: The Second Age lasted exactly 1,437 years and contained exactly three eras: - Era of Awakening — first era: 321 years, Second Age Years 1–321. Its lunar-magical aftermath included permanent loss of destroyed moon-specific powers, new magic from fragment-moons, and unpredictable/unreliable magical effects; civilizations learned not to depend exclusively on magic. - Era of Wonder — second era: 1,000 years, Second Age Years 322–1,321. Established character: magical renaissance and widespread prosperity across Eryndor after the darkness and confusion of the Era of Awakening. Peoples mastered new magics born of moon fragments and renewed civilizations' confidence in magical arts. This does not restore the permanently lost magics of the First Age or imply a universally conflict-free millennium. The Second Age Annals now establish some regional discoveries, rulers and events; the precise reason for Avarra’s cultural transition into the third era remains open. - Era of Fire — third era: 116 years, Second Age Years 1,322–1,437, as required by the fixed total. Its political and cultural history is now recorded in the Second Age Annals and Era of Fire chronicle; its final transition was the global earthquakes whose seismic waves reached the ancient Ironspine Mountains, were amplified tenfold worldwide through the range's deep roots and central position, and coincided with the creation/uplift of the far-western-tip Avarran mountains. These earthquakes ended the Second Age and began the Third Age; they did NOT create the Ironspine Mountains (which predate even the First Age). Safeguards: No surviving First Age records, and First Age had no eras. Do not confuse the three Second Age eras with worldwide Ages or automatically infer that all civilizations used the same era-naming calendars. Do not assign the First Throne, the separately established east–west war traditions, specific lunar magical disciplines or Gloin's ancestry to the Era of Wonder or Era of Fire by inference. Creator-authorized regional rulers and a distinct local Orundel water-rights conflict are now recorded for the Era of Fire, not retroactively for the Era of Wonder. The Era of Wonder's broad historical character as a millennium of worldwide prosperity and mastery of new magical forces is now established. Specific discoveries, named rulers and institutions, precise turning points and the event marking the transition to the Era of Fire remain to be developed. ## Era of Awakening — THREE simultaneous lunar-magical consequences, definitive correction (21 November 2026) Latest binding creator correction: The 321-year Era of Awakening at the start of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age was defined by all three, equally essential, transformations following the First Great Cataclysm: 1. PERMANENT LOSS: Before the Great Cataclysm, Eryndor had vastly more moons than the modern surviving roughly 221–255; the exact original count is unknown. When original moons were destroyed and their particular magical sources ceased to exist, entire associated forms of lunar magic were truly and irreversibly lost to Eryndor. These are not merely forgotten spells, temporarily weakened techniques, or powers awaiting rediscovery. Only First Age peoples could ever have witnessed or used certain such lost powers. No First Age records survive, so modern people cannot establish a reliable exhaustive roster or reconstruct those disappeared disciplines from intact original accounts. 2. BIRTH OF NEW MAGIC: Some fragments of shattered moons settled into new separate orbiting bodies — new “moons” — and became new sources of lunar magic with powers or disciplines not present before. The Cataclysm thus irreversibly reshaped the roster of lunar magics in both directions; it was simultaneously a destruction and a creation. The exact new-moon tally, identities, paths of formation, and individual disciplines remain unspecified. Other debris contributed to Eryndor's existing planetary rings; not every fragment becomes a magically potent moon. 3. UNRELIABILITY AND UPHEAVAL: In addition to those permanent changes, lunar magic was profoundly unstable and unreliable in the post-Cataclysm upheaval: some surviving powers fluctuated, faltered, became dangerous or unpredictable, and the newly arising lunar sources were poorly understood. Inconsistency and risk were a central reason many peoples learned that even powerful working magic could not be the only reliable foundation of agriculture, healing, infrastructure, water, food, defense, or daily survival. This does not force every existing power to fail everywhere at once or mean that all magic remains equally unstable forever. Different peoples' responses include nonmagical resilience, engineering, new magical inquiry and adaptations of existing traditions. Critical continuity: All three consequences matter, rather than replacing unreliability with lost/new magic or reducing permanently destroyed disciplines to temporarily unstable magic. The planet's independent Natural Magic / World's Breath remains extant; culturally distinct magical arts of Khazari, Eldar, Aelwyn, Gnomes, Pixies, etc. remain where they can function without annihilated lunar sources. The first Age lasted an unknown time, had no internal eras, and has no surviving records; it is only believed by later peoples to have been an exceptionally long age of prosperity. The specific count of moons destroyed, when and how fragments became stable new moons, and detailed lunar-magic mechanics are open. The moon-shattering, loss/birth of distinct powers, and instability are established as historical realities, even though surviving post-Cataclysm scholars may never have complete proof of every pre-Cataclysm discipline. Gloin's campaign remains paused at Autumn Day 22, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age, approximately 11:25 AM; the character has no new automatic knowledge of any secret location. ## Magical compatibility Disciplines have inherent affinities and degrees of compatibility. Some cooperate naturally, some require considerable skill to combine, and some resist or interfere with one another. Compatibility exists independently of lunar proximity. Aligned moons are not required for two disciplines to interact. Lunar conditions may strengthen or complicate an interaction, but they do not create its underlying compatibility. Illustrative affinities include: - Runecraft + Deepcraft: Structural and magical reinforcement. - Healing + Natural Magic: Restoration. - Elemental Magic + Nature Magic: Environmental workings. - Illusion + Divination: Perception and revelation. - Runecraft + protective or binding magic: Barriers and bindings. These examples are not a complete or universally fixed compatibility chart. The exact degree of compatibility, practical methods and risks depend on the disciplines, practitioner, working and conditions. ## Lunar imbalance and catastrophic risk When moons approach one another unusually closely, their magical influences can interfere, resonate or become unstable. Possible consequences include: - Excessive amplification or uncontrolled surges. - Unexpected interaction between disciplines. - Unstable enchantments and ancient mechanisms. - Disturbances in magical barriers or containment systems. - Changes in magical creatures and environmental conditions. - Regional or wider magical disruptions. An actual collision could produce a catastrophic magical imbalance. The destruction could release enormous magical energy and alter Eryndor's magical environment for centuries or millennia. It may also create new fragments, smaller moons and further orbital disturbances. These are possible consequences, not a guarantee that every close approach or collision produces an identical outcome. Lunar influence affects the whole world, not only spellcasters: magical creatures, enchanted objects, ancient structures, barriers and the natural environment may also be affected. Exceptional celestial conditions do not grant mastery automatically. A novice remains a novice; knowledge, training, aptitude, judgement and circumstances determine what can be achieved. ## The lost ancient art of Natural Magic harmonisation In ancient times, practitioners from several civilisations discovered sophisticated ways to harness and refine Natural Magic as a common medium between magical disciplines. This method did more than draw additional energy from the planet. Practitioners used Natural Magic as an intermediary to: - Strengthen magical workings. - Reduce resistance between disciplines. - Harmonise combinations that would otherwise be difficult. - Connect disciplines beyond their ordinary affinities. - Harmonise multiple lunar influences. - Create unified magical workings with greater efficiency than modern practitioners generally achieve. ### True fusion versus combined spellcasting True fusion is distinct from merely casting two spells together or using one discipline to support another. It creates a unified working from multiple disciplines, with Natural Magic serving as the common intermediary. The method did not eliminate the need for understanding, skill, control or judgement. It was a sophisticated technique, not a shortcut that allowed untrained people to combine any magic safely. ### Loss and possible survival Knowledge of the method was lost for unknown reasons. Possible explanations include civilisational collapse, catastrophe, deliberate suppression, destroyed infrastructure or incomplete fragments surviving without the original principles. None is established as the truth. Surviving traces may include ruins, manuscripts, instruments, incomplete teachings and oral traditions. ### Origins are not exclusively Khazari The method predates the First Throne and is not exclusively Khazari, dwarven or First Throne knowledge. Its first practitioners may have lived on any of Eryndor's five continents. Knowledge could have spread by trade, migration, conquest, exploration or cultural exchange; different civilisations may also have developed independent approaches. The most complete surviving knowledge may exist far from Avarra. Do not assume every relevant ruin or fragment on Avarra is connected to the First Throne. Gloin's hypothesis that Common or Natural Magic might act as an intermediary between specialised disciplines remains a developing personal hypothesis. He has not discovered the ancient method, its precise operation or its complete history. Elska's discreet research into historical attempts to use ambient or Common Magic as an intermediary is a separate research task; do not involve Hadrik in it without Gloin's choice. ## Peoples' distinct magical traditions survive the expanded cosmology (creator clarification, 21 November 2026) Binding distinction: The creator explicitly retains the different kinds of magic long associated with Khazari (dwarves), Eldar (elves), Aelwyn Fae, fairy peoples such as Pixies, Gnomes, and other peoples. These are legitimate distinct cultural, practical, possibly innate or supernatural traditions in the setting, not merely interchangeable labels for generic lunar spells. A tradition may have customary methods, ethics, rites, materials, aptitudes and histories, but the detailed disciplines and mechanisms outside already defined Khazari examples remain to be developed—not manufactured retrospectively. Do not merge Aelwyn Fae with Pixies/fairy folk, or make Gnome magic a copy of Khazari rune systems. Individual members of any people are not required to practise any tradition; cross-cultural learning and overlapping magic are possible when consistent with training and ability. Exact already-established Khazari traditions: Runecraft (symbols and enchantments); Deepcraft (stone, earth and subterranean perception/workings); Forgebinding (magical craft and durability); Hearthmagic (warmth, preservation, protection and domestic/settlement uses); Stonecalling (rare mountain-sense/communication); Ancestral Binding (controversial bloodline, oath and hereditary work). Keep them individually distinct, not automatically all lunar or inherently benevolent. Established broad fields include Arcana, Nature, Divination, Bloodcraft, Runecraft and Shadowcraft; these are not exhaustive nor species-exclusive. Moral aspect: Some magical forces are inherently good, some morally grey and some inherently evil, regardless of the caster's intentions. Do not assign an inherent moral alignment to an entire people, civilization, cultural school or broad discipline without specific creator definition; a tradition can contain different techniques and moral natures. This distinction adds nuance to the system without erasing Fae, fairy, Gnome, Eldar, Khazari or other magical heritage. Cosmic sources and knowledge: Moons are literal sources of lunar magic and people know that fact, but not how/why or which moon creates which magical force; some moons show almost no effects, others much stronger. Eryndor independently generates Natural Magic / the World's Breath. Gods of magic can govern or interact with magical forces, not replace moon magic as its source. Do not assign individual moons to cultural traditions or claim that all folk magic derives only from lunar forces without future decisions. Historical mystery, uncertainty and the paused Gloin scene remain protected. ## Recognised broad magical disciplines The setting already recognises broad disciplines including: - Arcana. - Nature. - Divination. - Bloodcraft. - Runecraft. - Shadowcraft. These are broad categories, not an exhaustive list of every discipline governed by every moon. The lunar roster remains unfinished. ## Khazari magical traditions Khazari practice includes specialised traditions. They are learnable through aptitude, training and work; they are not exclusive to nobility. 1. Runecraft: Symbols direct energy into objects and structures. It is used to enchant weapons, armour, buildings and mechanisms. 2. Deepcraft: Work with stone, earth and underground structures. Practitioners may sense weaknesses, water and subtle changes in rock, and manipulate small amounts of stone. 3. Forgebinding: Enchantment integrated with craftsmanship, producing durable weapons, self-maintaining edges and other crafted effects. 4. Hearthmagic: Warmth, preservation, protection and household or settlement workings. 5. Stonecalling: A rare tradition of communication or sensing with a mountain, including sensing movement through rock. Its limits and full practice remain to be developed. 6. Ancestral Binding: Controversial workings linked to bloodlines, oaths and hereditary obligations. The First Throne mastered this discipline. These traditions should not be treated as the only magic practised by Khazari, nor as the universal model for every other people. ## First Throne script and runic principles First Throne script is instruction-based. A symbol's meaning depends on its arrangement and context; the same symbol can function differently in another sequence. Three introductory symbols currently established in Gloin's study are: - Hold: Maintain a state or position. - Within: Define a boundary or enclosed space. - Until Command: A condition remains active until an authorised instruction is received. Together, an arrangement might express: “Maintain the enclosed state until an authorised command is received.” This does not prove that the command releases the enclosure; it might release, reinforce or change the system. Interpretation requires context, full sequence and technical understanding. ## Everyday and practical magic Magic is not confined to elite scholars, legendary heroes, royal courts or dangerous ancient mechanisms. It can have ordinary uses throughout Eryndor in farming, medicine, construction, transport, military service, crafts and household life. Examples of modest, specialised workings may include: - Preserving food or helping keep stores dry. - Warming a room or improving a lamp. - Detecting damp, disease or structural weakness. - Encouraging healthy soil or protecting crops. - Keeping tools in good condition. - Stabilising a wound or supporting medical care. - Purifying a small amount of water. - Reinforcing a shield or supporting field repairs. ### Practical limitations and access - A simple charm is not a substitute for every skill, tool or medical treatment. - A person may know a little practical magic without being a professional mage. - Some people use prepared charms or enchanted tools without being able to cast or fully understand the working. - Access varies with local culture, resources, cost, education, practitioners, laws, guilds and the strength of effect required. - A village healer may know a few useful workings; a wealthy city may support specialists, workshops and regulated magical services. - Magical aptitude is not the same as practical knowledge. Someone with little innate talent may learn simple procedures, while a naturally gifted person may lack the training to use that talent safely. - Magic can require time, concentration, materials, preparation, maintenance and recovery. It should not erase scarcity, expertise, injury, disease, labour or sound judgement. - Different peoples and regions develop their own ordinary magical practices. Khazari runic craft is one tradition, not the universal model. - Military magic may support signals, field repairs, protective work, medical care, detection and engineering, without turning every soldier into a battle-mage. Specific everyday spells, charms, tools, costs, regulations and regional customs will be developed as they become relevant. Their prevalence and sophistication vary across communities. ### Magic's effect on technological development Magic is one of the reasons Eryndor follows a different technological path from our own world. Practical workings and enchanted craft can fulfil some functions that might otherwise encourage the development of electrical systems, modern communications, industrial automation or other technologies. This changes the incentives and economic pressures that drive invention. Magic does not replace all engineering. Mechanical systems remain valuable where they are more reliable, scalable, economical or easier to maintain. Magitech combines physical engineering with runic or magical components, but still requires skilled labour, materials, maintenance and access to practitioners. This contributes to Eryndor's established technological boundary: high-medieval daily life, sophisticated regional engineering, and selected steam, hydraulic and magitech systems, without an automatic progression into modern or fully Victorian industrial society. This is a different path of development, not a world where invention has stopped. The detailed technological framework is recorded on the Technology, Craft & Infrastructure page. ## Magic canon boundaries - Natural Magic is always present; weak lunar influence does not mean magic vanishes. - Lunar orbital position, not phase alone, determines the strength of a moon's influence. - Each moon governs an individual discipline, but the complete roster remains open. - Compatibility exists independently of lunar alignment. - The lost Natural Magic harmonisation method is distinct from ordinary reinforcement or simultaneous spellcasting. - The lost method's origins, exact operation, surviving locations and reason for disappearance are unknown. - Gloin's theory remains his own developing hypothesis, not a confirmed rediscovery. - No new spell, discipline, moon-domain assignment, magical law or ancient technique becomes established simply because it would be convenient. Record new developments deliberately and with their evidence status.
